My name is not important, but I farm this small piece of land here in Dedza with my family. The soil is tired from many seasons of maize, so I must put something back or the harvest will be poor. I try to get fertilizer through the subsidy program when my name is on the list, and I also carry manure from my goats to the field because fertilizer alone is never enough for me. I cannot read, but I have farmed since I was a boy, and I know that on this small plot my own hands and my wife and children are what bring the food — I do not have money to pay other people.

I will plant hybrid seed this year because last season the armyworms and the dry spell hurt the local seed badly, and my neighbor's hybrid stood better. I intercrop with beans and pumpkin like always, so the soil is helped and we have relish. I have no way to bring water to the field — we wait for the rains like everyone here. For the armyworms I will try to use a little chemical if I can buy a small sachet at the market, because last year they ate into the cobs.
